The '''2010–11 La Liga''' (known as the ''Liga BBVA'' for sponsorship reasons) was the 80th season of [[La Liga]] since its establishment. The campaign began on 28 August 2010, and concluded on 21 May 2011. A total of 20 teams contested the league, 17 of which already partook in the [[2009–10 La Liga|2009–10 season]], and three of which were promoted from the [[2009–10 Segunda División|Segunda División]]. In addition, a new match ball – the Nike Total 90 Tracer – served as the official ball for all matches.<ref>{{cite news |title=Sergio Ramos presenta en Madrid el nuevo balón de la Liga, el 'T90 Tracer'|url=http://www.20minutos.es/noticia/797075/0/balon/liga/nike/|publisher=20 minutos |date=25 August 2010|access-date=2 July 2010|language=es}}</ref>

Defending champions [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] secured a third consecutive and overall 21st La Liga title following a 1–1 draw with [[Levante UD|Levante]] on 11 May 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/302109?cc=5739|title=Barca seal Spanish title|date=11 May 2011|work=ESPN|access-date=11 May 2011|archive-date=25 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121025195753/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/302109?cc=5739|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2011/may/11/levante-barcelona-live-la-liga|title=Levante v Barcelona – as it happened|date=11 May 2011|work=The Guardian|access-date=11 May 2011|location=London|first=Rob|last=Bagchi}}</ref> The result gave Barcelona a six-point lead with two matches remaining which, combined with their superior head-to-head record against [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]], ensured that they would finish top of the table.<ref>{{cite news|title=Barcelona crowned Spanish champions after Levante draw|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2011/SPORT/football/05/11/football.barcelona.messi.madrid/?hpt=T2|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110516155240/http://edition.cnn.com/2011/SPORT/football/05/11/football.barcelona.messi.madrid/?hpt=T2|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 May 2011|access-date=12 May 2011|newspaper=CNN International|date=11 May 2011}}</ref> Barcelona led the table since defeating Real Madrid 5–0 on 23 November 2010. From that point onwards, they lost only one match en route to winning the title.<ref>{{cite news|title=Barcelona win 2010–11 La Liga title|url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/3277/la-liga/2011/05/11/2482177/barcelona-win-2010-11-la-liga-title|access-date=12 May 2011|website=Goal.com|date=11 May 2011}}</ref> Barcelona's [[Lionel Messi]] won La Liga's [[LFP Awards|Award for Best Player]] for a third straight year.

The season was again dominated by Barcelona and Real Madrid, with second-place Madrid 21 points ahead of third-place [[Valencia CF|Valencia]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Barcelona Wins Third Straight Title to Extend Supremacy Over Real Madrid|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/2011-05-11/barcelona-wins-third-straight-title-to-extend-supremacy-over-real-madrid.html|access-date=12 May 2011|newspaper=Bloomberg|date=12 May 2011|first=Alex|last=Duff}}</ref> Having also faced off in the [[2010–11 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] semi-finals and the [[2011 Copa del Rey final|Copa del Rey final]], the top two [[El Clásico|rivals]] met four times over seventeen days, for a total of five meetings this season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Barca, Madrid To Battle Each Other 4 times in 17days|url=https://www.camisetasclubes.com/en/-ezp-29.html|access-date=12 May 2011|newspaper=League Update|date=13 April 2011}}</ref>

== Teams ==
[[Real Valladolid]], [[CD Tenerife]] and [[Xerez CD]] were relegated to the [[2010–11 Segunda División|Segunda División]] after finishing the [[2009–10 La Liga|2009–10 season]] in the bottom three places. Tenerife and Xerez made their immediate return to the second level after just one year in the Spanish top flight, while Valladolid ended a three-year tenure in La Liga.

The relegated teams were replaced by [[2009–10 Segunda División]] champions [[Real Sociedad]] from [[San Sebastián]], runners-up [[Hércules CF]] from [[Alicante]] and [[Levante UD]] from [[Valencia, Spain|Valencia]]. Hércules returned to the highest Spanish football league for the first time after 13 years, while Real Sociedad and Levante terminated their second-level status after three and two years, respectively.

=== Zamora Trophy ===
The [[Ricardo Zamora Trophy]] is awarded by newspaper ''[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]'' to the goalkeeper with the lowest ratio of goals conceded to matches played. A goalkeeper had to play at least 28 matches of 60 or more minutes to be eligible for the trophy.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/deporte/futbol/trofeos/2015-2016/zamora/primera.html|title=Trofeo Zamora La Liga Santander|work=Marca}}</ref>

=== Fair Play award ===
This award was given annually since 1999 to the team with the best fair play during the season. This ranking took into account [[La Liga#Competition format|aspects]]<ref name="La Liga fair play rules"/> such as cards, suspension of matches, audience behaviour and other penalties. This section not only aims to know this aspect, but also serves to break the tie in teams that are tied in all the other rules: points, head-to-head, goal difference and goals scored.

=== Overall ===
*Most wins - [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] (30)
*Fewest wins - [[UD Almería|Almería]] (6)
*Most draws - [[Sporting Gijón]] (14)
*Fewest draws - [[Real Sociedad]] (3)
*Most losses - [[Real Sociedad]] and [[Hércules CF|Hércules]] (21)
*Fewest losses - [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] (2)
*Most goals scored - [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] (102)
*Fewest goals scored - [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]] (31)
*Most goals conceded - [[UD Almería|Almería]] (70)
*Fewest goals conceded - [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] (21)
